label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Skier triggered size 2 and another skier remote triggered another size 2. Both on steeper, thinner more convex rocky terrain, not surprising to see.

reports.title: Helay Pass
reports.comment: avalanche: Size 2 skier triggered (may have been remote trigger, I saw it happen from pretty far away hard to know) 80cm crown, slid on 2.5mm facits. CT Sudden collapse at L12, triggered on a thin spot that also happened to be convex. Loud wumphing all day, lots of evidence of natural Avis size ~1.5-2 on similar slopes.

reports.title: Healy Pass- avalanches heard, not seen
reports.comment:
quick: Toured up to Healy Pass. Heard several large avalanches coming from the Egypt Lake area, couldn't see them due to poor visibility. 

Fresh, boot top powder on top of a fragile crust with facets underneath.

reports.title: Healy Pass area
reports.comment: quick: 25 cm of snow ontop a firmer layer; unconsolidated facets beneath that. Surface hoar found in the trees and protected areas. Increased winds on ridgetop. Found some good mellow skiing on West aspects and wind sheltered areas.

reports.title: Monarch Ramparts East
reports.comment: quick: We rode some of the short slopes on the east side of Monarch Ramparts. Poked around other aspects which were wind hammered. Probed 150 cm at the top of the slope in the photo and found around 50 cm mid slope after loosing a ski to a rock and boot packing back up. Foot penetration to ground made for easy boot packing.

reports.title: Simpson Slide Paths Avalanche Control Results
reports.comment: quick: Avalanche control results from the Simpson area slidepaths. Conditions were not as touchy here as on Whymper, but still produced slabs with most shots. Generally, results were smaller than on Whymper, but still deep, just less propagation. The exception to this was a wide, deep slab on our Simpson 3 avalanche path that failed on a steep convex roll at treeline. This was ~ 80 cm deep and fai…

reports.title: Simpson Burn
reports.comment: quick: Skied the Simpson burn up to ~1900m. 10cm of new on a supportive mid pack higher but endless facets in the steeper rocky terrain. 5cm MFcr lower down on the surface and very punchy and grabby. 50cm at the road and lots of deadfall still showing but decent coverage after 1400m. No signs of instability but stuck to conservative terrain. Some evidence of small slides down the slide paths and t…

reports.title: Vermillion Crossing
reports.comment: quick: Skied mellow trees in the Vermillion Burn. Coverage started marginal and steadily improved with elevation. Basal facets were readily apparent and failed easily in hand shears. We therefore avoided slopes over 30 degrees and overhead hazard. The day was mainly cloudy and warm, with the sun occasionally showing.

reports.title: Simpson Burn
reports.comment: quick: Pretty outrageous few days in Simpson Burn. The cold, still nights have consolidated upper elevation snow well, and made for prime riding conditions. Worked our way into steeper terrain over a couple days with no signs of instability and premium pow. Definite surface hoar development, will have to monitor this interface for next storm cycle. As interloping Americans, we felt so very pleased…

reports.title: Vermillion range
reports.comment: quick: Lots of natural activity on south aspects through out the vermillion range some being cornice triggered other looked to be solar triggered, most went close to ground. A few of the roadside paths between Simpson and Floe had point releases that ran full path.

reports.title: Mount Verendrye East Burnt Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Good skiing! Morning 10 and 30 cm quick uptrack cut tests were stable, but once it began to warm up under the sun, these began to fail (around 15 cm deep). We stayed on angles 30° and less.

It looked like a few of the upper chutes had some size ~1 releases probably from cornice failures recently. These ran around 30-50 m.

reports.title: 93 S
reports.comment: quick: We saw remnants of a slide today at Serac down one of the north facing gullys. Looked like it happened some time this morning between our runs. We stayed stricly in the trees and had some nice turns.  Wet snow on East and Southeast facing slopes up to 1950 m.  Lots of solar radiation, even with temps hovering around -10C.  Top 5 cm  affected.

reports.title: Simpson area
Serac creek avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: A few days old now but still notable deep slab in one of the gullies on the Serac Ridge. Maybe triggered by a cornice. Failed on the ground level within the burnt trees and ran a long way down the gully .

reports.title: Serac
reports.comment: quick: Did a few yoyo laps on upper serac. -15 at car to start and by 1:30 was +6/7 at car. Breakable crust for bottom 150m, crust didn’t soften by the end. Upper east facing pitches (above 1500/1600m) the snow was un impacted despite sun and heat. Observed some debris in slide paths but didn’t witness any activity. Sun was certainly intense.

reports.title: Vermillion crossing
reports.comment: quick: 2-10cm MFcr up to ~1550m decreasing with elevation. Facets below the crust to the ground until 1600m where a bit of a mid pack started to form. Snow improved with elevation, did a quick pit at 1950m in an open patch NE aspect. See snowpack tab for details.
